newsitem.title: UK: Shell refutes human rights case claims.
newsitem.headline: Shell refutes human rights case claims.

text.p: Royal Dutch Petroleum Co and Shell Transport and Trading Co refuted claims filed in a U.S. lawsuit that the companies played a role in the hanging of two Nigerian human rights activists, a spokesman said.

The spokesman said the company had "not been given notice" of the lawsuit but had seen a press release from the Centre for Constitutional Rights which filed the suit in Manhattan federal court under the Alien Tort Claims Act.

The suit was brought by the families of Ken Saro-Wiwa, who was the leader of the Movement for Survival of Ogoni People and John Kpuinen, deputy president of the group's youth wing on the first anniversary of their deaths.
"Those (allegations)have been refuted previously and they are further refuted now," the Shell spokesman said.

The families allege the two were killed because of their challenges to the military dictatorship of Sani Abacha and to Shell's role in human rights violations in Nigeria, including environmental destruction.
